issue.title: Chart data API recomputes the full query for every dashboard filter change
issue.body:
Problem: every native-filter change on a dashboard issues one `POST /api/v1/chart/data` per chart and each request rebuilds the SQLAlchemy query from scratch in `superset/common/query_context_processor.py`. On a dashboard with 30 charts a single filter click causes 30 full query builds and 30 cache lookups, which currently takes 4 to 6 seconds before the first chart repaints.

Expected outcome: a filter change on the same dashboard repaints the first chart in under a second because query construction for unchanged form data is reused. Existing `/api/v1/chart/data` responses stay byte-identical for the same inputs.

Evidence: `superset/common/query_context_processor.py::get_df_payload` shows up as 70% of request time in a `py-spy` profile taken while clicking a filter; the profile is attached to the linked discussion https://github.com/apache/superset/discussions/1.

Acceptance criteria: the profile share of query construction drops below 20% on the same dashboard and the `tests/integration_tests/charts/data` suite passes unchanged.

This touches the architecture of the query context layer, so the triage session should describe the smallest bounded change and flag anything that would be a breaking change for API clients.
